result.proposed_fix:
(1) snapshot.js page text: give consecutive visible text nodes that share the same block-level container, with no
or block boundary between them, the same group id (only bump textGroup when the nearest block ancestor changes or a
intervenes), so finish() and onscreen.join concatenate them with "" and the existing whole-vs-pieces check in finish() collapses a cross-node secret into one masked piece. Build `text`/chunks the same way: mask the concatenation per block, not per node. (2) Headings: visibleTextOf joins inline-adjacent nodes with "" and uses one group for them, the same as the selection path. (3) Python defence in depth: before redact_text in perception (text, headings, labels, values), join pieces of inline-adjacent groups without a separator. Or, in _url_parts/urlParts in both layers, fail closed: when a token ends with a secret-naming 'key=' (empty value), a bare secret-naming key followed by an '=' token, or 'scheme://user:' with no '@', mask the following token. (4) Add a self-contained Chromium regression embedding the R42-01 HTML (, key/value, / userinfo, password,

with session_id), for no_selection and ctrl_a, asserting no secret appears in the Brain body. Add Python unit cases for the \n- and space-split forms.
result.root_cause:
The URL secret rule added for R41-03 (_url_parts in redact.py:162-175, applied per _TOKEN [^\s"'<>]+ at redact.py:139; urlParts/maskText in snapshot.js:45-62) masks one whitespace-free token at a time. The page-text and heading pipelines put a separator between every DOM text node: snapshot.js:474 gives each text node its own group (textGroup++) and calls finish(...,"
"); snapshot.js:472/552 masks each node alone (chunks.push(maskText(t))) and joins chunks with "
"; headings use visibleTextOf with one group per node and parts.join(" ") (snapshot.js:481-484), then finish(ps," ") (snapshot.js:488). In Python, onscreen.join (onscreen.py:383-394) puts sep between groups, and perception masks the already-separated string (perception.py:184 with "
", perception.py:138/144 with " "). An inline element boundary (<b>, <span>, <em>, <a>) inside a URL therefore becomes whitespace, so 'client_secret=' (empty value, skipped by `if not m.group(3)`) and the value 'ZqSPLIT...' are separate tokens, and 'https://alice:' never matches the userinfo regex because '@' is in the next token. finish() (snapshot.js:348-356) compares the masked joined text using the same separator, so it cannot see a secret split across nodes either. The selection path joins nodes with "" (snapshot.js:530-533, perception.py:171/179), which is why it masks the same URL.
result.why_earlier_repairs_failed: Only repair 12 (78006f9) addressed R41-03; repairs 1-11 predate it (R1-04 in ca622bc added redact_url/maskUrl for the Location only). 78006f9 added _url_parts/urlParts as a last per-token pass in redact_text/maskText. It left the input unchanged: page text and headings stayed split per text node with \n or space separators, both in snapshot.js and in perception/onscreen.join. Its regressions (tests/assist/test_a0_r41_review_regressions.py:83-104 Chromium page, :144-156 redact_text cases) only put each URL in a single text node, so the inline-split forms were never tested.
